**Verdict: fix_first**

The contract does not appear to contain an obvious unrestricted drain, but it has several deployment-blocking and correctness issues.

| Severity | Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---|
| **High** | 431–442 | **`launchLPs()` cannot initialize liquidity from the minted supply.** `_mint()` sends all tokens to the owner at lines 428–429, while `launchLPs()` adds `balanceOf(address(this))` tokens. Unless the owner first transfers tokens to the contract, this value is zero and Uniswap V2 liquidity creation will normally revert because of `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY`. Add an explicit funding/initialization flow or have `launchLPs()` transfer tokens from the owner. |
| **High** | 431–442 | **`launchLPs()` has no one-time guard.** It can be called repeatedly. After the first successful launch, `createPair()` will revert because the pair already exists. Add `require(address(uniswapV2Router) == address(0))` or equivalent initialization state. |
| **High** | 566–574, 622–628 | **Swap processing can be triggered with an uninitialized router.** The owner can enable swapping before calling `launchLPs()`. If the contract has any token balance, a later transfer can call `swapAndLiquify()`, which dereferences the uninitialized `uniswapV2Router` and reverts. Require router/pair initialization before enabling swaps or before swapping. |
| **High** | 566–574, 622–628 | **`swapAndLiquifyByLimitOnly` can permanently revert transfers.** The code triggers swapping whenever `contractTokenBalance > 0`, but if limit-only mode is enabled it sets `contractTokenBalance = minimumTokens` even when the contract owns fewer tokens. The router then attempts to transfer more tokens than the contract owns. Require the balance to be at least `minimumTokens`, or use `min(balance, minimumTokens)`. |
| **High** | 468–484, 531–536 | **Transfers to the burn address can unexpectedly revert.** When an excluded account transfers to `0xdead`, `liqBurnAt()` executes. It performs `liquidityPairBalance.sub(minimumTokens)`. Before LP initialization, or whenever the pair has less than `minimumTokens`, this underflows and reverts. A normal transfer to the burn address should not depend on LP state. |
| **High** | 468–484 | **`liqBurnAt()` burns almost the entire LP token balance.** It transfers `pairBalance - minimumTokens` from the pair to `deadAddress`, then calls `sync()`. This is a highly destructive and unusual behavior, and it is triggered by a transfer to `0xdead`, not by an explicit owner-only operation. Confirm that this is intended and protect it with clear, dedicated logic. |
| **Medium** | 464–466 | **`burn()` is broken.** It calls `_transfer(msg.sender, address(0), amount)`, but `_transfer()` rejects zero recipients at lines 527–529. Also, there is no `_totalSupply` decrement anywhere, so even a working burn would not reduce reported total supply. |
| **Medium** | 369–385 | **The advertised 2% tax is not actually configured.** All buy/sell fee components are initialized to zero, and the constructor calculates `_totalTaxIfBuying` and `_totalTaxIfSelling` from those zero values. The public totals therefore remain zero. If 2% taxation is intended, initialize the fee components or provide controlled setters with bounds. |
| **Medium** | 377–386, 633–638 | **Distribution settings have no functional effect.** `_liquidityShare`, `_marketingShare`, `_teamShare`, and `_totalDistributionShares` are not used by `swapAndLiquify()`. All swapped ETH is sent to `teamWallet` at lines 633–638. |
| **Medium** | 633–635 | **ETH forwarding uses `transfer()`.** `wallet.transfer(amount)` can fail for contract wallets or wallets whose fallback requires more than the 2,300-gas stipend, potentially blocking swaps and therefore token transfers. Use a checked low-level call instead. |
| **Medium** | 628–630 | **Swaps use zero slippage protection.** `swapExactTokensForETHSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens(..., 0, ...)` allows the swap to receive any amount of ETH and is vulnerable to sandwiching/poor execution. Use a configurable minimum output or an oracle/quote-based bound. |
| **Medium** | 431–442 | **The router is hardcoded to the Ethereum Uniswap V2 router.** Deployment on any other chain, or on a fork with a different router, will fail or interact with an unintended address. Pass the router in the constructor or validate the deployment network. |
| **Medium** | 431–442, 398–401 | **Trading and liquidity initialization are operationally fragile.** `tradingActive` starts false, while liquidity setup depends on the owner and exemptions. Test the exact sequence—fund contract, launch LP, enable trading, and configure swap settings—before deployment. |
| **Low/Design** | 650–657 | **Owner has extensive unilateral control.** The owner can change wallet limits, transaction limits, exemptions, AMM pair designations, swapping behavior, and trading activation. This is not an exploit by itself, but it should be disclosed or governed by a multisig/timelock if trust minimization is intended. |
| **Low** | Throughout | **`SafeMath` is redundant under Solidity 0.8.19.** This is not a security issue, but it adds complexity and gas overhead. |

Before deployment, at minimum:

1. Fix the LP initialization and add a one-time initialization guard.
2. Prevent swaps before router initialization.
3. Fix the limit-only swap logic.
4. Remove or redesign the implicit `liqBurnAt()` behavior.
5. Correct `burn()`, including total-supply accounting.
6. Confirm and implement the intended tax/distribution model.
7. Replace ETH `.transfer()` and add swap slippage protection.
8. Test the full launch and trading lifecycle on a fork.
